transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Yeah... well, honestly, it took a lot for me to even make this appointment. I just... I really need some help, because things have gotten really out of hand. I work as a mechanic, right? Down at the auto shop, and it’s a tough environment, you’re always on your feet, always moving, so you'd think I wouldn't worry about this stuff, but... well, what's been happening is, I’ll eat too much. Like, way, way too much. I'll just lose it and eat everything in sight. And then this massive wave of panic hits me because I am just completely terrified of gaining weight. I mean, at 45, it’s not like the weight just falls off anymore, you know? 

So, to fix it, I’ve been going into the bathroom and... well, I make myself throw up. I just force myself to get sick so I won't put on any pounds. And I used to tell myself I was in control, like it was just a quick fix if I overdid it on a bad day, but now... I'm doing it all the time. I'll be scrubbing the motor oil and grease off my hands just so I can go into the shop bathroom and throw up. It’s exhausting. And the scariest part, the real reason I'm sitting here today, is that it's gotten to the point where I'm genuinely scared I can't stop doing it. I try to stop, I tell myself every morning that today is the day I just eat a normal meal and leave it alone, but I can't. I just end up right back in the bathroom, over and over, and I don't know how to break the cycle.
How often do you have these episodes where you eat too much and then make yourself throw up?

Well, doctor, if I really sit down and think about it... it's been going on like this for a while now. I mean, for at least the past three months, honestly, there’s hardly been a single week where I didn’t have one of those episodes. You know, where I just completely lose control and eat everything in sight, usually late at night when the house is quiet and I'm just sitting there with my thoughts. And then, of course, the panic sets in, and I have to go make myself throw up afterward. 

And it's not just a once-in-a-while thing anymore. Some weeks, it happens several times. It's especially bad when I’m home more. See, I have this bad back—occupational hazard, you know, from bending over engines and lifting heavy parts all day at the shop. When my back flares up and I have to take time off or just can't move around much on the weekends, I'm just stuck at home. And being stuck at home means I'm closer to the kitchen, and I get bored, or anxious, or frustrated about my back, and before I know it, I'm just eating and eating. And then I'm in the bathroom again. It's just this constant, exhausting cycle, week in and week out, for months now. I just... I can't seem to get a break from it.
Is your fear of gaining weight what drives you to make yourself throw up after eating too much?

Yeah. Yeah, it is. It's exactly that. I mean, I'm just terrified of it. It's like this constant, looming threat, you know? Because... well, I step on that scale in the bathroom, and even if it's just one pound—just one single pound up—my heart just starts racing. I completely panic. It's like my brain just short-circuits. I start thinking about all that time I've been spending laid up on the couch with my bad back, not moving around the shop, not lifting the heavy tools, and I just think, "Oh my god, it's happening. I'm turning soft. I'm losing all my strength and just getting fat." 

And the minute I see that number go up, even a fraction, it's like a switch flips in my head. I can't even think straight. All I can focus on is how to undo it. I start planning it out right then and there—what I can skip eating, or how soon I can get to the bathroom if I do eat, just to get rid of it. It's like this desperate need to just hit the reset button, to empty it all out so that pound doesn't stick. Because if one pound sticks, then what's to stop five pounds, or ten? It's just... it's exhausting, being so afraid of my own body changing, especially when my back is already making me feel so useless. So, yeah, the throwing up... it's the only way I feel like I can stop it from happening.
Do you do anything else to try to compensate for the weight you might gain after eating too much, besides making yourself throw up?

No, no, it's really just the throwing up. I know some people, you know, they talk about taking pills or running for hours and hours, but I don't do any of that. Honestly, with my back the way it is, I couldn't run even if I wanted to. Just standing under a lift at the shop for a few hours leaves me needing a hot pack and a handful of ibuprofen, so exercise is pretty much out of the question. And I don't mess with laxatives or anything like that. I've heard horror stories about those, how they mess up your insides, and I just... I don't want to go down that road. 

Plus, the throwing up... it just feels more immediate, you know? Like, the panic hits, and I know exactly how to fix it right then and there. I don't have to wait for a pill to kick in or try to drag myself through a workout when my lumbar spine is screaming at me. I just go to the bathroom, and it's done. It's horrible, and I hate it, and my throat is always sore, and my teeth feel sensitive, but it's the only thing I do. I just... I rely on it completely to fix the mistake of eating too much. So, yeah, no other stuff. Just that one terrible habit that I can't seem to break.
Have you ever had episodes where you ate too much and didn't make yourself throw up afterward?

No, no, I don't think I ever do that. I mean, if I eat like that—if I have one of those moments where I just completely lose it and eat everything—I *have* to get rid of it. There is just no way I could... I don't know, go to sleep or go back to watching TV with all that food sitting in my stomach. It feels so heavy, you know? Like this actual lead weight just dragging me down from the inside. 

I think maybe once, a long time ago, I tried to just ride it out. I told myself I was just going to drink a big glass of ice water, go to bed, and try to forget about it, but I was just laying there in the dark, sweating, with my heart pounding out of my chest. All I could think about was every single bite just sitting there, digesting, turning into fat while I was just laying there useless on the mattress. I don't think I lasted more than twenty minutes before I was up and in the bathroom. 

It's like... the anxiety just builds and builds until I feel like my skin is crawling. It's not even just the physical feeling of being stuffed, though honestly that feels awful too, it's the mental part of it. It's the knowing exactly what I just did and feeling so disgusted with myself. So, no, I never just leave it. The panic is just way too strong for me to ignore. I always, always end up making myself sick. I just can't handle the guilt otherwise. I have to finish the cycle, or I wouldn't be able to function at all the next day. I'd just be standing under a car at the shop, staring at a transmission or holding a wrench, completely distracted, just beating myself up over what's inside me. So I always make sure it's gone.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating during these episodes where you eat too much?

No... no, not at all. That's the scariest part, honestly. It's like... it's like I'm not even driving the car anymore, you know? I'm just sitting in the passenger seat watching it crash. Once I start on those nights, usually after a really bad day where my back has just been killing me and I've been struggling to get through the shift at the shop... I'll come home, and I'll open the pantry, and it's like my brain just disconnects. 

My hands just keep grabbing food, pulling out boxes of cereal, bags of chips, whatever is there. And the whole time, there's this little voice in my head, like, right in the back of my mind, screaming, "Lucy, knock it off! What are you doing? Stop! You're going to regret this!" But it's like I can't hear it, or I can't listen to it. My hands are moving faster than my thoughts. I'll be tearing into packaging, barely even tasting what I'm putting in my mouth, just chewing and swallowing as fast as I can. 

It's this frantic, desperate feeling, like I'm starving, even though I'm not. I'm just... I don't know, trying to fill up some empty space or numb out the pain in my back or just stop thinking about how useless I feel lately. And I don't feel back in charge, like I'm actually back in my own body, until it's already done. Until all the wrappers are empty and my stomach is stretched so tight it hurts, and that panic I told you about starts setting in. That's when the control comes back, but by then, it's too late. The damage is done, and then I have to go to the bathroom and fix it. But during the eating? No. Zero control. It's terrifying.
Do you usually feel guilty or ashamed after these episodes of eating too much?

Oh, god, yes. The guilt is... it's overwhelming. It's almost worse than the physical feeling of being so full. I mean, the second I stop eating, the second I realize what I've just done and look at all the empty wrappers and boxes on the counter, this massive wave of shame just crashes over me. It's like I can't even look at myself in the mirror. I just feel so pathetic, you know? 

I'm a grown woman. I work hard, I rebuild engines, I fix things that are broken, but I can't even fix this one thing about myself. I can't even control what goes into my own mouth. And the shame... it just eats at me. I'll be in the bathroom, leaning over the toilet, and I'm just crying, sometimes not even realizing I'm crying until the tears are hitting the porcelain, just thinking, "Why are you like this, Lucy? Why can't you just be normal?" 

And it doesn't just go away after I throw up, either. The physical panic might ease up a bit, but the guilt? That sticks around. I'll wake up the next morning, and my throat will be raw, and I'll be getting dressed for work, putting on my uniform, and I just feel dirty. Like I'm keeping this horrible, disgusting secret from everyone at the shop. The guys will be joking around, asking what I had for dinner the night before, and I just have to smile and lie and say, "Oh, just a salad," or whatever, while inside I'm just burning with shame because of what I really did. It's exhausting, honestly. It's just this constant, heavy blanket of guilt that I'm dragging around with me every single day. I just feel so broken.
Have you ever had an episode where you ate a large amount of food in a short time and didn't make yourself throw up afterward?

Well, like I was saying just a minute ago, I really don't ever keep it down. I just can't. But if you're asking if the amount of food is really that large, and if it happens fast? Yes. Oh, absolutely yes. It's... it's honestly staggering how much I can put away when I get into one of those states. 

It almost always happens at night after everyone’s gone quiet. The whole house is just dead silent, the neighborhood is asleep, and I’m usually just so physically exhausted from standing on the concrete floor at the shop all day. I won't even turn all the lights on. I’ll just stand in the kitchen—I don't even bother to pull out a chair and sit down at the table, I just stand right there in the glow of the open fridge or under the stove light—and eat leftovers, cereal, chips, ice cream, whatever’s there. 

I'll bounce from salty to sweet and back to salty again. I'll eat an entire Tupperware container of cold pasta right out of the plastic, and then immediately open a family-sized bag of potato chips and just inhale them, and then I'll move on to a whole carton of butter pecan ice cream. It goes way, way past a normal meal. I'm not eating because I'm hungry for dinner, you know? It's just this frantic shoveling of food into my mouth, one thing after another, in such a incredibly short window of time. I'll just keep going and going until half the pantry looks completely picked over. You'd think a teenager had a party or like a tornado went through the shelves. 

So, yes, it is a massive amount of food, and it all happens in maybe thirty or forty minutes. But like I said before, I never, ever let it stay in my stomach. The second I realize how much I've just consumed and look at the wreckage in the kitchen, that panic sets in, and I have to go to the bathroom to get rid of it. I've never just eaten all of that and gone to sleep.
Have you ever used diuretics or laxatives to try to compensate for the weight you might gain after eating?

Pills? Like laxatives or... no, no, I don't mess with any of that. I've never bought diuretics or anything. For me, it's... well, like I've been saying, it's always the throwing up. That's my way of fixing it. 

Honestly, the whole reason I finally made this appointment and came in here today is because of that. After I eat too much, I just... I keep making myself throw up in the bathroom because I am so absolutely terrified of gaining weight. I mean, my knees and my lower back already take such a beating at the shop, bending over hoods and crawling under chassis all day. If I actually kept all those thousands of calories down and put on a bunch of weight, I wouldn't even be able to do my job. My body would just give out. So I have to get it out of me. I go in there, I turn on the exhaust fan so it's loud, I run the faucet, and I just force myself to be sick until my stomach is completely empty.

But the thing is... the thing that really pushed me to sit in this chair and talk to you, is that I'm scared I can't stop doing it anymore. It’s gotten to where it’s not even a choice. I’ll be kneeling there on the bathroom tiles, my throat is raw, sometimes there's even a little blood, my chest hurts, and I'll promise myself, "Lucy, this is it. This is the absolute last time. Never again." I mean it with my whole heart in that moment. But then the next night rolls around, I get stressed, I eat, and the exact same thing happens. I'm just locked in this cycle of making myself sick so I won't get fat, and I have zero brakes left. I'm just terrified I'm going to be doing this every single night for the rest of my life and I don't know how to turn it off.
How many times a week do you have these episodes of eating too much?

Oh, man. How many times a week? It's... well, it's a lot. If I'm really looking at it, for at least the past three months, there's hardly been a single week where I didn't have one of those late-night eating episodes and then go make myself throw up afterward. I mean, I can't even remember the last time I went a full seven days without doing it. 

And honestly, it's usually way more than just once. Some weeks it happens several times... especially lately, when I’m home more because of my back. I mentioned earlier how much of a beating my body takes at the shop, right? Well, my lower back has been acting up so badly lately that I've had to take some extra time off just to ice it and rest. And when I'm stuck at home like that, just sitting around off my feet... I don't know, the boredom and the stress of missing work just kind of eat at me. I'll be on the couch, my back is throbbing, the house is quiet, and my brain just goes straight to the kitchen. 

It's like the more time I have on my hands, the worse it gets. I'll end up doing it three, maybe four times in a week when I'm laid up like that. It's been this solid, relentless cycle for months now, every single week without fail. I keep hoping, you know, maybe this week I'll just have a normal dinner and go to sleep, but... no. It just hasn't happened. I'm just constantly fighting it, and constantly losing.
How many times do you typically make yourself throw up in a week?

Well, I guess it’s exactly what I was just telling you about the eating, because the two things... they never, ever happen apart. If I have one of those massive late-night eating episodes, I am absolutely, one hundred percent going to make myself throw up right afterward. It's a package deal for me. 

So, like I was saying just a second ago, for at least the past three months, there really hasn't been a single week where I didn't go through that whole routine. Not one. And the throwing up... it's several times a week, just like the eating, especially on those weeks when my back is flared up and I’m stuck at home off my feet. If I'm eating like that three or four times because I'm stuck on the couch stressing about missing work at the shop, then I'm in the bathroom throwing up three or four times. 

I just can't separate them, you know? I can't have a night where I eat all that food and just say, "Oh well, I'll do better tomorrow," and go to sleep. My brain doesn't work like that anymore. The second the food is in there and I realize what I've done, that horrible panic hits my chest, and I'm right back over the toilet, turning on the exhaust fan so no one hears me, running the tap, and forcing it all back up. It’s exhausting, it really is. It wipes me out completely. But yeah, to give you a number, it's several times a week, every single week, for at least three months now.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short time without subsequently making yourself throw up?

No. No, never. Like I said, they are a package deal. I mean, I honestly can't even fathom doing that. Just... sitting there with all that food inside me? All those thousands of calories just sitting in my stomach, digesting, turning into fat? God, my skin is crawling just thinking about it. 

If I ate like that—all those chips and the entire sleeve of cookies and the ice cream, just shoveling it in while I'm sitting on the couch with my back aching—and then I didn't go to the bathroom afterward? I would lose my mind. The panic would literally swallow me whole. I'd be pacing a hole in the floorboards. I wouldn't be able to sleep, I wouldn't be able to breathe right. I'd just be thinking about my joints, my knees, my lower back, how I'm going to ruin my body and lose my job at the shop because I got too heavy to crawl under a truck. 

So, no. If the binge happens, the throwing up happens. Every single time. There's no scenario where I eat like that and just let it stay down. It's like a reflex at this point. The second I take that last bite and realize what I've done, the guilt is so heavy I can barely stand it, and I'm practically sprinting to the bathroom to turn the fan on and get it out of me. I can't leave it in there. I just can't.
Do you ever experience a loss of control during episodes of eating a normal or slightly larger than normal amount of food?

Yeah, that’s exactly the problem, because that’s almost always how it starts. I’ll go into the kitchen thinking, okay, I’m just going to have a regular sandwich, or maybe just one bowl of cereal. You know, a totally normal amount of food. I’ll be standing there, usually leaning against the counter because my lower back is just screaming at me after being bent over an engine block all day, and I’ll eat that normal portion. But then... I don't know, it's like a switch flips inside my brain. 

Once I start on those nights, it doesn't even matter that it was supposed to be a normal meal. It’s like my hands just keep grabbing food, completely on their own. I'll be reaching into the pantry for the chips, then the cookies, and in my head, I am literally fighting myself. I’m standing there telling myself, "Lucy, knock it off. Put the bag down, you don't need to do this, go back to the couch." But my hands just aren't listening to my brain. 

It is the most terrifying, helpless feeling, like I’ve been shoved into the passenger seat of my own body. I’m just watching myself tear open packages and shovel it in, and I can't hit the brakes. The chewing, the swallowing, reaching for the next thing... it’s all just pure autopilot. And I honestly don’t feel back in charge until it’s already done. It’s not until the food is gone and I’m just standing there in the middle of the kitchen, feeling so stuffed and disgusted with myself, that I finally feel like I have the steering wheel back. So, yeah, even if I try to just eat a normal dinner, the control just vanishes the second I take that first bite.
Have you ever used excessive exercise as a way to try to compensate for the weight you might gain after eating too much?

No, I... I can't really do that. I mean, I wish I could, sometimes I think it would be better if I could just go run it off like some people do, you know? But with my back... it's just not an option. Being a mechanic, especially for as long as I have, it just ruins your body. My lower back is a wreck, my knees ache when it rains, and my shoulders pop every time I lift my arms above my head. 

I've been working at the shop since I was in my twenties, right out of high school, and bending over those engines, crawling on the concrete floors, hauling tires around... it takes a toll. So by the time I get home, I'm usually just icing my back and trying to find a position on the couch that doesn't make me want to cry. 

The idea of going for a run or doing some kind of crazy workout after a binge... it's just physically impossible for me. If I tried to do jumping jacks or run a mile, I wouldn't be able to walk the next day, let alone get to work. And I can't miss work. I need this job. So, no, exercise isn't my go-to. I just... I stick to the throwing up, because it's the only thing I can actually manage to do to get rid of it all without putting more strain on my joints. It's awful, but it's all I've got.
Do you ever experience episodes of eating too much without subsequently engaging in any compensatory behaviors like making yourself throw up?

I feel like you just asked me that, didn't you? Or maybe I'm misunderstanding the question... but no. Like I was saying a minute ago, I never, ever just keep the food down. That’s actually the whole reason I’m here sitting in this office with you today. Because after I eat too much, I keep making myself throw up in the bathroom so I won’t gain weight, and it’s gotten to where I’m honestly scared I can’t stop doing it. 

I mean, I used to think I was completely in control of it. I'd tell myself, "Okay, Lucy, you messed up, you ate the whole box of cookies, just go take care of it so you don't pack on the pounds." Because like I said, I absolutely cannot afford to get heavy. My back is already a disaster from twenty-odd years of leaning over engine bays and crawling under cars. If I gain weight, my knees will give out, my back will completely spasm, and I'll lose my livelihood. I won't be able to turn wrenches anymore. So I started doing it just to manage the weight. 

But now? Now it doesn't feel like a choice anymore. It's like this horrible, mandatory routine. I go into the bathroom, I turn on the exhaust fan so the neighbors in the apartment next door don't hear anything, I pull my hair back, and I just do it. And I'm doing it so much now. It’s like my entire evening revolves around this awful cycle of eating and then getting rid of it, and it's so exhausting. I wake up the next morning and my throat is raw, my eyes are all puffy, and I just feel so defeated. I really am terrified that I'm going to be stuck doing this for the rest of my life, because I feel completely powerless to stop it now. So, no, there is never an episode where I don't throw up. I always do. I have to.
Is making yourself throw up the only method you use to try to compensate for the weight you might gain after eating too much?

Yeah, I mean, like I was just saying... it's just the throwing up. I know I keep repeating myself, but it really is the only thing I do. I don't take pills or anything like that. I've never messed with laxatives or diuretics, mostly because, honestly, I'm at the shop all day. I can't be running to the bathroom every five minutes when I'm supposed to be doing a brake job or dropping a transmission, you know? My boss would fire me in a heartbeat if I was constantly off the floor. 

So it's just the throwing up. That's the whole reason I finally made this appointment. Because, like I mentioned, after I eat too much, I just keep making myself throw up in the bathroom so I won't gain the weight. And it's just... it's taken over everything. I'll be at work, my hands covered in grease, and I'll catch myself thinking about what I'm going to eat when I get home, and then how I'm going to get rid of it. It's like this sick routine that I can't break out of. 

I used to think, "Oh, I'll just do this once in a while, just when I really overdo it." But now, it's every time. Every single time I have one of those episodes where I lose control, I end up in the bathroom. And I'm just so scared now because I really feel like I can't stop doing it. It's like my brain tells me I have to do it, or else my back is going to give out from the weight, and I'll lose my job, and I'll lose everything. So, yeah, it's just the throwing up, but it's... it's enough to completely ruin my life.
How often do you have episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating?

Well, it's... it's a lot. I mean, if I really sit down and think about it, looking back over, say, the last three months or so? There's hardly been a single week where I didn't have one of those episodes. You know, the late-night ones where I just completely lose it, eat everything in sight, and then have to go into the bathroom and make myself throw up afterward. 

It's almost always at night. I get home from the shop, my back is just screaming at me from being hunched over all day, and I'm so exhausted I can barely see straight. I'll sit down on the couch with my ice pack, turn on the TV just for some background noise, and then... I don't know, it's like a switch flips in my head. I start eating to try and comfort myself, I guess, or distract myself from the pain, and before I know it, I've eaten way too much and I'm panicked. 

And some weeks, it's not just once or twice. Some weeks it happens several times. It's usually worse when my back is acting up really badly and I end up having to stay home more, or if I'm just stuck on the couch all weekend because I can't move. Being idle like that, just sitting there in pain, it just makes the urge to eat so much stronger. And then, of course, the panic sets in about gaining weight and ruining my joints even more, so I end up right back over the toilet. It's just... it's constant. Like I said, for the past three months at least, it's been pretty much every single week, multiple times a week. It never really stops.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you make yourself throw up after eating too much?

Oh, absolutely. I mean, it's the entire reason. Like I keep saying, I just... I cannot afford it. It's to the point where, well, I have this scale in my bathroom, right? And if I step on it in the morning and see even just one single pound up on that bathroom scale, I just completely panic. It's this immediate, cold sweat kind of panic. 

It makes me feel like all that time I spent laid up on the couch with my back acting up is just... it's turning me soft, you know? Like my body is just giving up and I'm losing my edge. And the second I see that number go up, before I can even think straight or even process anything, I'll start planning exactly how to undo it. My mind just starts racing—like, "Okay, what am I going to do tonight to fix this? How do I make sure this doesn't stick?" 

It’s exhausting, honestly. Because in the shop, if you go soft, if you put on extra pounds, you can't maneuver under a lift, you can't bend over a fender for three hours without your lower lumbar screaming at you. Every extra pound is just more pressure on joints that are already shot to hell from twenty years on concrete floors. So yeah, the fear of gaining weight is... it's everything. It drives the whole cycle. If I wasn't so completely terrified of putting on the weight and ruining my back for good, I wouldn't be forcing myself to get sick in that bathroom every night. I just wouldn't.
Have you ever had an episode where you ate a large amount of food in a short time without feeling the need to make yourself throw up afterward?

Well, I mean... no, not really. Because, see, the throwing up is always the end of it. It's the whole point of fixing the mistake. But I guess... well, if you're asking about the eating part itself, like what that actually looks like before I end up in the bathroom... yeah, I do eat a massive amount of food all at once. 

It usually happens at night. Like, late at night, after my husband has gone to bed and the house is just totally quiet. I'll be sitting there with my ice pack, like I said, and then I just... I get up and go into the kitchen. And I'll just stand there. I don't even sit down at the table or put things on a plate half the time. I just stand there in the kitchen and eat whatever is in front of me. Leftovers from dinner, bowls of cereal, half a bag of potato chips, straight from the bag, then maybe I'll dig into a carton of ice cream. It's just whatever is there, whatever I can get my hands on quickly. 

And I'll just keep eating, way, way past what a normal person would eat for a meal, or even two meals. I just keep going until I feel physically sick from how full I am. It's like a blur, honestly. Next thing I know, I'm looking around and half the pantry looks completely picked over, like a raccoon got into it or something. And the guilt... it's just immediate. The second I stop eating and realize what I've done, the panic sets in about my back and my job, and that's when I have to go to the bathroom. So, the eating part definitely happens, that huge amount of food in a short time, but I always, always have to throw it up afterward. I can't just let it sit there. I'd lose my mind.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because after I eat too much, I keep making myself throw up in the bathroom so I won’t gain weight, and it’s gotten to where I’m scared I can’t stop doing it.

patient.answer:
Hi, doctor. Yeah... well, honestly, it took a lot for me to even make this appointment. I just... I really need some help, because things have gotten really out of hand. I work as a mechanic, right? Down at the auto shop, and it’s a tough environment, you’re always on your feet, always moving, so you'd think I wouldn't worry about this stuff, but... well, what's been happening is, I’ll eat too much. Like, way, way too much. I'll just lose it and eat everything in sight. And then this massive wave of panic hits me because I am just completely terrified of gaining weight. I mean, at 45, it’s not like the weight just falls off anymore, you know? 

So, to fix it, I’ve been going into the bathroom and... well, I make myself throw up. I just force myself to get sick so I won't put on any pounds. And I used to tell myself I was in control, like it was just a quick fix if I overdid it on a bad day, but now... I'm doing it all the time. doctor.question: How often do you have episodes where you feel like you've lost control while eating?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: For at least the past three months, there’s hardly been a week where I didn’t have one of those late-night eating episodes and then go make myself throw up afterward. Some weeks it happens several times, especially when I’m home more because of my back.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the frequency of the episodes involving a loss of control while eating, which directly corresponds to the criteria for how often binge eating and compensatory behaviors occur.

patient.answer:
Well, it's... it's a lot. I mean, if I really sit down and think about it, looking back over, say, the last three months or so? There's hardly been a single week where I didn't have one of those episodes. You know, the late-night ones where I just completely lose it, eat everything in sight, and then have to go into the bathroom and make myself throw up afterward. 

It's almost always at night. I get home from the shop, my back is just screaming at me from being hunched over all day, and I'm so exhausted I can barely see straight. I'll sit down on the couch with my ice pack, turn on the TV just for some background noise, and then... I don't know, it's like a switch flips in my head. I start eating to try and comfort myself, I guess, or distract myself from the pain, and before I know it, I've eaten way too much and I'm panicked. 

And some weeks, it's not just once or twice. Some weeks it happens several times. It's usually worse when my back is acting up really badly and I end up having to stay home more, or if I'm just stuck on the couch all weekend because I can't move. Being idle like that, just sitting there in pain, it just makes the urge to eat so much stronger. And then, of course, the panic sets in about gaining weight and ruining my joints even more, so I end up right back over the toilet. It's just... it's constant. Like I said, for the past three months at least, it's been pretty much every single week, multiple times a week. It never really stops.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's fear of gaining weight is the primary motivator for their purging behavior
doctor.question: Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you make yourself throw up after eating too much?

target_item.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
target_item.manifestation: Even a pound up on the bathroom scale makes me panic like all the time I spent laid up with my back is turning me soft, and I’ll start planning how to undo it before I can think straight.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question explicitly asks about the fear of gaining weight as the primary motivation for the purging behavior, which aligns directly with the Fear_of_Weight_Gain symptom.

patient.answer:
Oh, absolutely. I mean, it's the entire reason. Like I keep saying, I just... I cannot afford it. It's to the point where, well, I have this scale in my bathroom, right? And if I step on it in the morning and see even just one single pound up on that bathroom scale, I just completely panic. It's this immediate, cold sweat kind of panic. 

It makes me feel like all that time I spent laid up on the couch with my back acting up is just... it's turning me soft, you know? Like my body is just giving up and I'm losing my edge. And the second I see that number go up, before I can even think straight or even process anything, I'll start planning exactly how to undo it. My mind just starts racing—like, "Okay, what am I going to do tonight to fix this? How do I make sure this doesn't stick?" 

It’s exhausting, honestly. Because in the shop, if you go soft, if you put on extra pounds, you can't maneuver under a lift, you can't bend over a fender for three hours without your lower lumbar screaming at you. Every extra pound is just more pressure on joints that are already shot to hell from twenty years on concrete floors. So yeah, the fear of gaining weight is... it's everything. It drives the whole cycle. If I wasn't so completely terrified of putting on the weight and ruining my back for good, I wouldn't be forcing myself to get sick in that bathroom every night. I just wouldn't.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's behavior is more aligned with bulimia nervosa or binge eating disorder by asking about the presence of binge eating episodes without compensatory behaviors
doctor.question: Have you ever had an episode where you ate a large amount of food in a short time without feeling the need to make yourself throw up afterward?

target_item.name: Eating_Large_Amount
target_item.manifestation: At night after everyone’s gone quiet, I’ll stand in the kitchen and eat leftovers, cereal, chips, ice cream, whatever’s there, way past a normal meal until half the pantry looks picked over.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about episodes of eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, which corresponds to the symptom of eating a large amount (binge eating).

patient.answer:
Well, I mean... no, not really. Because, see, the throwing up is always the end of it. It's the whole point of fixing the mistake. But I guess... well, if you're asking about the eating part itself, like what that actually looks like before I end up in the bathroom... yeah, I do eat a massive amount of food all at once. 

It usually happens at night. Like, late at night, after my husband has gone to bed and the house is just totally quiet. I'll be sitting there with my ice pack, like I said, and then I just... I get up and go into the kitchen. And I'll just stand there. I don't even sit down at the table or put things on a plate half the time. I just stand there in the kitchen and eat whatever is in front of me. Leftovers from dinner, bowls of cereal, half a bag of potato chips, straight from the bag, then maybe I'll dig into a carton of ice cream. It's just whatever is there, whatever I can get my hands on quickly. 

And I'll just keep eating, way, way past what a normal person would eat for a meal, or even two meals. I just keep going until I feel physically sick from how full I am. It's like a blur, honestly. Next thing I know, I'm looking around and half the pantry looks completely picked over, like a raccoon got into it or something. And the guilt... it's just immediate. The second I stop eating and realize what I've done, the panic sets in about my back and my job, and that's when I have to go to the bathroom. So, the eating part definitely happens, that huge amount of food in a short time, but I always, always have to throw it up afterward. I can't just let it sit there. I'd lose my mind.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms align with bulimia nervosa, characterized by recurrent episodes of binge eating followed by compensatory behaviors, such as self-induced vomiting, to prevent weight gain. The patient's fear of gaining weight and the frequency of these episodes meet the diagnostic criteria for bulimia nervosa.
